notes: This is a single typescript continuation page with 26 baseline text lines, two raised typed insertions, six cancellation locations (one phrase spans two lines), one underlined R, and an archive pencil number 37. There is no authorial page number, title, dateline, signature, standalone display, drawing, or diagram.

The page describes locally an association of coverings to inertia-group representations, states a description of Galois coverings through commuting left G_i and right H actions on H-torsors, gives Hom(G_i,H)/H for isomorphism classes, and claims that this description proves an indicated full-faithfulness criterion. These are document claims; the unspecified geometric criterion was not checked.

The final paragraph acknowledges an interpretation of the Kummer case in example 3 and names divisibility as the intended order relation between n-prime and n. The physical interval is blank; no relation sign is supplied.

The exact retained forms include makes a sense, stricly, and convevient. Mixed or obscured forms remain explicit: rather/rahher; reallization/realization; pocal/local; s/f and o/i in the first two cells of sormulation; mihd/mind. Interior automorphism is singular as printed. Abbreviations i.e. and mod. are not expanded.

No written question mark or authorial doubt annotation appears. Reader uncertainty is distinguished from the author’s cancellations and overtyping. Readable cancelled th, restr, l, and classified were recovered; systems and the r/hyphen cancellation remain uncertain.

The upper and lower ink around the G of Galois is represented approximately by accent commands, without interpreting the marks as intentional accents. For the group capital, G and H contours coexist; double-struck G is not established. No order of unlike-letter overprinting is assigned.

The mathematical context suggested looking carefully at the group letter and the n-prime/n gap, but did not decide their ink. The later right H action was not used to force H in the earlier mixed cell. The explicit mention of divisibility was not used to insert a symbol.

The two interlinear additions were inspected with their punctuation and baseline surroundings. The first is assigned after E.; the second is placed after means, as the best spatial reading, with attachment relative to the comma still doubtful. No punctuation was moved from one physical line to another as an assumed correction.

The whole image and each original half were displayed once. Seventeen local crops were made with Pillow autocontrast and LANCZOS to 2600 pixels across, without sharpening or rotation; each was displayed once. No OCR, recognition, internet research, other pages, or another reader’s material was used. No crop was remade.

The archive sheet number is not counted as an H omission; the witness/page-number conventions are treated semantically. Ordinary line-break hyphens in analogous, commuting, and convevient were joined; the lexical hyphen before functor is retained with its visible preceding space.

checks.statement: For groups K and H, commuting left K and right H actions on a nonempty right H-torsor are classified up to equivariant isomorphism by Hom(K,H)/H. For the page’s finite-set situation this applies when H is finite.
checks.outcome: Verified the algebraic assertion directly: choose e in E and define rho(k) by k.e = e rho(k). Commutation gives rho(k1 k2) = rho(k1)rho(k2). Replacing e by e h changes rho to h^{-1}rho h. Conversely a homomorphism acts on the right torsor H by left multiplication through rho; equivariant torsor isomorphisms give precisely these conjugacies. This checks the displayed classification under its torsor hypotheses, not the unspecified geometric realization or full-faithfulness claims, and it did not decide any ambiguous ink.
